moments.selftext: BREAKING: Short interest in the median S&P 500 stock is up to 3.2% of market cap, the highest level since 2009. This is now approaching the 2008 Financial Crisis peak of ~3.8%. By comparison, during the 2022 bear market, this percentage was ~1.7%. Furthermore, short interest among the most heavily shorted 10% of S&P 500 stocks is up to 8.0% of market cap, the highest in 8 years. Even during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst, short interest never surged to these levels. The short trade is starting to look overcrowded.

moments.selftext: BREAKING: Global broad money supply surged +$10.7 trillion YoY in June, or +7.7%, to a record $150 trillion. This marks the 9th consecutive YoY increase above +7.0%, the longest such streak since 2021. The biggest increase over this period was recorded in February 2026, at +11.9%. Since 2000, global money supply has risen +$124 trillion, a +6.9% compounded annual growth rate over this period. Since 2020 alone, money supply has surged +$50 trillion, or +50%, equivalent to an average increase of ~$7.5 trillion per year. Global money creation is expanding at a historic pace.

moments.title: The Romans built this vast underground water palace beneath Constantinople. Beneath modern Istanbul lies the Basilica Cistern, an enormous underground reservoir constructed during the reign of Eastern Roman Emperor Justi
moments.selftext: The Romans built this vast underground water palace beneath Constantinople. Beneath modern Istanbul lies the Basilica Cistern, an enormous underground reservoir constructed during the reign of Eastern Roman Emperor Justinian I in the sixth century. Although it is commonly called Byzantine, the people who built it considered themselves Romans, and Constantinople was still the capital of the Roman Empire in the East. The cistern supplied water to the Great Palace and surrounding buildings, helping the city endure droughts, damaged aqueducts, and prolonged sieges. Its cathedral-like interior measures roughly 453 feet long and 213 feet wide, with a brick ceiling supported by 336 marble columns arranged in 12 rows of 28. Each column rises nearly 30 feet from the floor. Many of the columns were salvaged from older Roman structures, which explains why their materials, dimensions, and decorative capitals vary so much. Water reached the cistern through a network of channels and aqueducts stretching into the countryside beyond Constantinople. When full, the reservoir could hold around 80,000 cubic meters, or more than 21 million gallons, of water. After the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453, the cistern gradually fell out of regular use and was largely forgotten. Local residents reportedly continued lowering buckets through openings in their floors, sometimes pulling up water and even fish from the darkness below. Perhaps its strangest features are two enormous reused carvings of Medusa’s head beneath the columns. One is positioned sideways and the other upside down. The exact reason remains uncertain, but the orientations may have helped the ancient blocks function as stable bases for the columns.

moments.selftext: “The mirror is my best friend because when I cry, it never laughs.” - Charlie Chaplin Charlie Chaplin (1889–1977) was an English comic actor, filmmaker, composer, and one of the most influential figures in the history of cinema. Born on 16 April 1889 in London, he rose from a childhood of poverty to become one of the most recognizable stars of the silent-film era. Best known for his iconic character “The Tramp,” Chaplin used comedy to explore poverty, loneliness, inequality, and the resilience of the human spirit. His films, including The Kid, The Gold Rush, City Lights, Modern Times, and The Great Dictator, combined humor with genuine emotion and continue to captivate audiences worldwide. Chaplin was far more than a performer. He wrote, directed, produced, and composed music for many of his films, giving him remarkable creative control over his work. He helped transform cinema by showing that comedy could be both hilarious and deeply moving. Chaplin died on 25 December 1977, but his influence has endured. His distinctive style, timeless humor, and belief in the power of human compassion continue to inspire filmmakers, actors, and audiences across generations.

moments.title: YESTERDAY, I SPENT 4 HOURS WITH CHATGPT CLEANING UP MY ONLINE IDENTITY. RESULT: 39 EXPOSED PROFILES FOUND. 16 OLD LOGINS CLOSED. 5 PUBLIC MENTIONS BURIED. HOW I DID IT, STEP BY STEP:￼
moments.selftext: YESTERDAY, I SPENT 4 HOURS WITH CHATGPT CLEANING UP MY ONLINE IDENTITY. RESULT: 39 EXPOSED PROFILES FOUND. 16 OLD LOGINS CLOSED. 5 PUBLIC MENTIONS BURIED. HOW I DID IT, STEP BY STEP:￼
thread: 1/ Start with a search by full name Most people think they are “private” until they are properly searched on Google. I used my real name, old usernames, old email addresses, and common misspellings. Search for your name on Google, Bing, social media platforms, forums, image search, and username search sites.

2/ Map all old usernames Your old usernames are often the real leak. A 2016 gaming username can connect with Reddit, GitHub, forums, markets, and dead social accounts. Give ChatGPT all the usernames you remember and ask it to create a search checklist by platform type.

3/ Find the dead accounts first Old accounts are dangerous because you forgot what they show. Links in the bio, profile pictures, old comments, bad jokes, public likes, abandoned portfolios. Open each exposed profile and sort it into 3 buckets: delete, private, update.

4/ Remove personal details I wasn't trying to disappear. I was trying to eliminate easy connections between my name, location, email, job, and old posts. Delete or edit public mentions of your city, birthday, workplace, school, old emails, and linked accounts.

5/ Clean Search Results Some things cannot be removed instantly. That's why I updated more solid profiles to boost cleaner results above old mentions. Update your main LinkedIn, X, Threads, website, Medium, GitHub, or portfolio profile with clean and consistent information.￼

6/ Close forgotten logins This part seems boring until you realize how many applications still have your data. Old newsletters, forums, tools, marketplaces, job boards, free trials, random SaaS accounts. Search your email inbox for “welcome”, “verify”, “confirm your account”, “reset password”, and “login”.

7/ Block what remains online Not all accounts need to be deleted. The accounts you keep should be harder to hijack and harder to connect to each other. Enable two-factor authentication, remove public email addresses, change weak passwords, unlink old applications, and review privacy settings.
